executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)

```zsh
brew install go-critic
```

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)

```zsh
sudo port install go-critic
```

## Usage

Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.

Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.

```
Supported sub-commands:
	check - run linter over specified targets
		$ go-critic check -help
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='paramTypeCombine,unslice' strings bytes
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./...
	version - print linter version
		$ go-critic version
	doc - get installed checkers documentation
		$ go-critic doc -help
		$ go-critic doc
		$ go-critic doc checkerName
```

### Examples

```bash
# Runs all stable checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check fmt

# Run all stable checkers on `pkg1` and `pkg2`
go-critic check pkg1 pkg2

# Run all stable checkers on `fmt` package and configure rangeExprCopy checker
go-critic check -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold 128 fmt

# Runs specified checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check -enable elseif,paramName fmt

# Run all stable checkers on current dir and all its children recursively:
go-critic check ./...

# Like above, but without `appendAssign` check:
go-critic check -disable=appendAssign ./...

# Run all stable checkers on `foo.go` file:
go-critic check foo.go

# Run stable diagnostics over `strings` package:
go-critic check -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental' strings

# Run all stable and non-opinionated checks:
go-critic check -enableAll -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./src/...
```

> To get a list of available checker parameters, run `go-critic doc <checkerName>`.

### Checker Tags

In place of a single name, **tag** can be used. Tag is a named checkers group.

Tags:

* `#diagnostic` - kind of checks that detect various errors in code
* `#style` - kind of checks that find style issues in code
* `#performance` - kind of checks that detect potential performance issues in code
* `#experimental` - check is under testing and development. Disabled by default
* `#opinionated` - check can be unwanted for some people. Disabled by default
* `#security` - kind of checks that find security issues in code. Disabled by default

## Documentation

For complete documentation and a full list of checkers, visit [go-critic.com](https://go-critic.com/overview).
</output>

rangeExprCopy checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [performance]

Detects expensive copies of `for` loop range expressions.

Suggests to use pointer to array to avoid the copy using `&` on range expression.

Non-compliant code:
var xs [2048]byte
for _, x := range xs { // Copies 2048 bytes
	// Loop body.
}

Compliant code:
var xs [2048]byte
for _, x := range &xs { // No copy
	// Loop body.
}

See Go issue for details: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/15812.

Checker parameters:
  -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold int
    	size in bytes that makes the warning trigger (default 512)
  -@rangeExprCopy.skipTestFuncs bool
    	whether to check test functions (default true)
</output>

# Let me compute levenshtein distances
python3 << 'EOF'
def levenshtein(s1, s2):
    m, n = len(s1), len(s2)
    dp = [[0]*(n+1) for _ in range(m+1)]
    for i in range(m+1): dp[i][0] = i
    for j in range(n+1): dp[0][j] = j
    for i in range(1, m+1):
        for j in range(1, n+1):
            if s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]:
                dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]
            else:
                dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1])
    return dp[m][n]

cmds = ["check", "doc", "help", "version"]

for t in tests:
    dists = [(levenshtein(t, c), c) for c in cmds]
    dists.sort()
    print(f"{t!r}: {dists}")
EOF

package checkers

func init() {
	initCheckers()
}

func initCheckers() {
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "appendAssign",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic"},
		Summary: "Detects suspicious append result assignments.",
		Before: "p.positives = append(p.negatives, x)\np.negatives = append(p.negatives, y)",
		After: "p.positives = append(p.positives, x)\np.negatives = append(p.negatives, y)",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "appendCombine",
		Tags: []string{"performance"},
		Summary: "Detects `append` chains to the same slice that can be done in a single `append` call.",
		Before: "xs = append(xs, 1)\nxs = append(xs, 2)",
		After: "xs = append(xs, 1, 2)",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "argOrder",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic"},
		Summary: "Detects suspicious arguments order.",
		Before: `strings.HasPrefix("#", userpass)`,
		After: `strings.HasPrefix(userpass, "#")`,
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "assignOp",
		Tags: []string{"style"},
		Summary: "Detects assignments that can be simplified by using assignment operators.",
		Before: "x = x * 2",
		After: "x *= 2",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "badCall",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic"},
		Summary: "Detects suspicious function calls.",
		Before: "strings.Replace(s, from, to, 0)",
		After: "strings.Replace(s, from, to, -1)",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "badCond",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic"},
		Summary: "Detects suspicious condition expressions.",
		Before: "for i := 0; i > n; i++ {\n\txs[i] = 0\n}",
		After: "for i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\txs[i] = 0\n}",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "badLock",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic", "experimental"},
		Summary: "Detects suspicious mutex lock/unlock operations.",
		Before: "mu.Lock(); mu.Unlock()",
		After: "mu.Lock(); defer mu.Unlock()",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "badRegexp",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic", "experimental"},
		Summary: "Detects suspicious regexp patterns.",
		Before: "regexp.MustCompile(`(?:^aa|bb|cc)foo[aba]`)",
		After: "regexp.MustCompile(`^(?:aa|bb|cc)foo[ab]`)",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "badSorting",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic", "experimental"},
		Summary: "Detects bad usage of sort package.",
		Before: "xs = sort.StringSlice(xs)",
		After: "sort.Strings(xs)",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "badSyncOnceFunc",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic", "experimental"},
		Summary: "Detects bad usage of sync.OnceFunc.",
		Before: "sync.OnceFunc(foo)()",
		After: "fooOnce := sync.OnceFunc(foo); ...; fooOnce()",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "boolExprSimplify",
		Tags: []string{"style", "experimental"},
		Summary: "Detects bool expressions that can be simplified.",
		Before: "a := !(elapsed >= expectElapsedMin)\nb := !(x) == !(y)",
		After: "a := elapsed < expectElapsedMin\nb := (x) == (y)",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "builtinShadow",
		Tags: []string{"style", "opinionated"},
		Summary: "Detects when predeclared identifiers are shadowed in assignments.",
		Before: "len := 10",
		After: "length := 10",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "builtinShadowDecl",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic", "experimental"},
		Summary: "Detects top-level declarations that shadow the predeclared identifiers.",
		Before: "type int struct {}",
		After: "type myInt struct {}",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "captLocal",
		Tags: []string{"style"},
		Summary: "Detects capitalized names for local variables.",
		Before: "func f(IN int, OUT *int) (ERR error) {}",
		After: "func f(in int, out *int) (err error) {}",
		Params: []Param{
			{Name: "paramsOnly", Type: "bool", Doc: "whether to restrict checker to params only", Default: true},
		},
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "caseOrder",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic"},
		Summary: "Detects erroneous case order inside switch statements.",
		Before: "switch x.(type) {\ncase ast.Expr:\n\tfmt.Println(\"expr\")\ncase *ast.BasicLit:\n\tfmt.Println(\"basic lit\") // Never executed\n}",
		After: "switch x.(type) {\ncase *ast.BasicLit:\n\tfmt.Println(\"basic lit\") // Now reachable\ncase ast.Expr:\n\tfmt.Println(\"expr\")\n}",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "codegenComment",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic"},
		Summary: "Detects malformed 'code generated' file comments.",
		Before: "// This file was automatically generated by foogen",
		After: "// Code generated by foogen. DO NOT EDIT.",
	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "commentFormatting",
		Tags: []string{"style"},
		Summary: "Detects comments with non-idiomatic formatting.",
		Before: "//This is a comment",

	})
	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "commentedOutCode",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic", "experimental"},
		Summary: "Detects commented-out code inside function bodies.",
		Before: "// fmt.Println(\"Debugging hard\")\nfoo(1, 2)",
		After: "foo(1, 2)",
		Params: []Param{
			{Name: "minLength", Type: "int", Doc: "min length of the comment that triggers a warning", Default: 15},
		},

	registerChecker(&CheckerInfo{
		Name: "commentedOutImport",
		Tags: []string{"style", "experimental"},
		Summary: "Detects commented-out imports.",
		Before: "import (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t//\"os\"\n)",
		After: "import (\n\t\"fmt\"\n)",
	})

		Name: "defaultCaseOrder",
		Tags: []string{"style"},
		Summary: "Detects when default case in switch isn't on 1st or last position.",
		Before: "switch {\ncase x > y:\n\t// ...\ndefault: // <- not the best position\n\t// ...\ncase x == 10:\n\t// ...\n}",
		After: "switch {\ncase x > y:\n\t// ...\ncase x == 10:\n\t// ...\ndefault: // <- last case (could also be the first one)\n\t// ...\n}",
	})

		Name: "deferInLoop",
		Tags: []string{"diagnostic", "experimental"},

	})

func runChecker(info *checkers.CheckerInfo, pkg *linter.Package, f *ast.File, params *CheckerParams) []Warning {
	ctx := &linter.CheckContext{

package main

import "fmt"
import "go/ast"
import "go/parser"
import "go/token"

func main() {
	src := `
package foo

func test() {
	x := *new(bool)
	_ = x
}
`
	fset := token.NewFileSet()
	f, _ := parser.ParseFile(fset, "test.go", src, 0)
	
	ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		unary, ok := n.(*ast.UnaryExpr)
		if !ok || unary.Op != token.MUL {
			return true
		}
		fmt.Printf("UnaryExpr(*) found: %T\n", unary.X)
		call, ok := unary.X.(*ast.CallExpr)
		if !ok {
			fmt.Println("Not a call expr")
			return true
		}
		fn, ok := call.Fun.(*ast.Ident)
		if !ok {
			fmt.Printf("Not ident: %T\n", call.Fun)
			return true
		}
		fmt.Printf("Function: %s, args: %d\n", fn.Name, len(call.Args))
		if fn.Name == "new" && len(call.Args) == 1 {
			fmt.Printf("Found *new(%T)\n", call.Args[0])
		}
		return true
	})
}
</output>

func checkParamTypeCombine(ctx *CheckContext, f *ast.File, params *checkParams) []Warning {
	var warnings []Warning
	checkFuncType := func(ft *ast.FuncType, pos token.Pos, funcStr string) {
		if ft.Params == nil {
			return
		}
		// Check if consecutive params have the same type
		canCombine := false
		var prevType ast.Expr
		for _, field := range ft.Params.List {
			if len(field.Names) == 0 {
				prevType = nil
				continue
			}
			if prevType != nil && formatNode(field.Type) == formatNode(prevType) && len(field.Names) > 0 {
				canCombine = true
				break
			}
			prevType = field.Type
		}
		if canCombine {
			warnings = append(warnings, warn(pos, "%s could be replaced with combined params", funcStr))
		}
	}
	ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		switch x := n.(type) {
		case *ast.FuncDecl:
			if x.Type.Params != nil {
				checkFuncType(x.Type, x.Pos(), formatFuncDecl(x))
			}
		}
		return true
	})
	return warnings
}

func formatFuncDecl(fn *ast.FuncDecl) string {
	var parts []string
	if fn.Type.Params != nil {
		for _, field := range fn.Type.Params.List {
			names := make([]string, len(field.Names))
			for i, n := range field.Names {
				names[i] = n.Name
			}
			parts = append(parts, strings.Join(names, ", ")+" "+formatNode(field.Type))
		}
	}
	return "func(" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")"
}
